Schotten, Tobias Pfandzelter, David Bermbach, Arndt Kritzner, Enrico Zschau, Prasenjit Dhara, Steve G\"oring, William Menz, Alexander Raake, Wolfgang R\"uther-Kindel, Fabian Quaeck, Nick Stuckert, Robert Vilter

item.title: Multistatic ISAC with Deep Learning-Based Clutter Suppression for 5G and Beyond
item.description: arXiv:2610.40586v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) systems using 5G and beyond signals of opportunity enable joint wireless sensing and communication using shared infrastructure and spectrum resources. While multistatic ISAC can increase sensing coverage with spatially distributed receivers, dense and dynamic clutter can significantly degrade bistatic range and Doppler estimation, leading to errors in target localization and velocity estimation. This paper presents a multistatic ISAC framework with clutter suppression for high-fidelity estimation of target position and velocity. Distributed clutter is modeled with randomly located scatterers with varying Doppler spreads and radar cross sections to capture dense and dynamic clutter effects. A broad range of conventional signal processing baselines are evaluated for clutter suppression, showing limited robustness under strong clutter conditions. To address this limitation, deep learning-based clutter suppression methods are introduced to improve robustness against dense and dynamic clutter by employing residual and attention-enhanced deep neural network architectures that directly enhance target responses from clutter-contaminated observations. These methods substantially outperform conventional approaches in target position and velocity estimation across diverse clutter conditions in multistatic ISAC.
item.dc:creator: Yalin E. Sagduyu, Tugba Erpek, Sastry Kompella

item.title: Generalized Graph Signal Sampling by Difference-of-Convex Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2306.14634v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a comprehensive framework for the generalized sampling and recovery of graph signals by leveraging difference-of-convex (DC) optimization. A fundamental challenge in graph signal processing is sampling, especially for graph signals that are not bandlimited. To accurately capture complex real-world phenomena, it is essential to handle beyond bandlimited graph signals, moving past traditional bandlimited assumptions. Consequently, extending the generalized sampling theory to graph signals has been studied, enabling the best possible recovery for a wide range of signals by assuming signal priors. However, achieving the best possible recovery requires handling inherently non-convex and computationally intractable constraints such as the full rank constraint. As a result, existing methods have relied on either aggressive convex relaxations that sacrifice accuracy or greedy algorithms that risk falling into poor suboptimal solutions, facing a fundamental dilemma between modeling accuracy and optimization tractability. To overcome this dilemma, we propose a DC optimization-based method for designing an aggregation sampling operator for beyond bandlimited graph signals that comprehensively handles arbitrary signal priors assumed in the generalized sampling theory. Specifically, the intractable full rank constraint is relaxed using the nuclear norm, reformulating the design problem into a DC optimization problem. We develop a solver based on the general double-proximal gradient DC algorithm, which theoretically guarantees convergence to a critical point. Experimental results on synthetic and real-world data demonstrate the superiority of our method in sampling and recovering beyond bandlimited graph signals compared to existing approaches (see https://www.mdi.comp.isct.ac.jp).
item.arxiv:journal_reference: IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing, vol. 74, pp. 4653-4667, 2026
item.dc:creator: Keitaro Yamashita, Kazuki Naganuma, Shunsuke Ono

item.title: Two-Stage Rotation-Based Joint ToA-AoA Estimation for Spatial Wideband Systems
item.description: arXiv:2503.18111v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Joint delay-angle (time-of-arrival (ToA) and angle-of-arrival (AoA)) estimation in wideband multi-antenna orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems is a key enabler for localization, sensing, and extremely large-multiple input multiple output (XL-MIMO) communications in mmWave/THz bands. In this regime, the spatial wideband effect (SWE), also known as range-angle coupling in MIMO frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar, breaks the conventional spatial narrowband assumption; the energy of each path is spread over multiple delay-angle bins, and the dominant peak of the 2D-DFT spectrum no longer coincides with the true coarse grid location. As a result, standard DFT-based coarse estimation followed by rotation/maximum-likelihood fine-tuning becomes inherently biased. In this paper, we first develop a rigorous finite-dimensional characterization of this phenomenon. Using a 2D Dirichlet-kernel model, we derive closed-form bounds on the SWE-induced spreading width and show that the significant energy of a single path is confined to at most $\lceil \alpha M |\tilde{\phi}_i| \rceil$ bins in both angle and delay, where $\alpha$ denotes the fractional bandwidth, $M$ the array size, and $\tilde{\phi}_i$ the normalized AoA of the $ i$-th scatterer. Building on this analysis, we propose a two-stage per-path rotation framework. In the first stage, we apply a cluster-level removal of the wideband coupling term and perform a localized 2D search to correct the SWE-induced coarse-bin shift. In the second stage, we show that the residual wideband term is uniformly bounded and can be treated as a small perturbation; this justifies a narrowband-type rotation refinement that yields super-resolution off-grid estimates of AoA, ToA, and path gains with near-DFT complexity.

item.title: Sampling Method for Generalized Graph Signals With Pre-Selected Vertices via DC Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2509.14836v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper proposes a method for vertex-wise aggregation sampling of a broad class of graph signals, designed to attain the best possible recovery based on the generalized sampling theory. This is achieved by designing a sampling operator by an optimization problem, which is inherently non-convex, as the best possible recovery imposes a rank constraint. An existing method for vertex-wise aggregation sampling is able to control the number of active vertices but cannot incorporate prior knowledge of mandatory or avoided vertices. To address these challenges, we formulate the operator design as a problem that handles a constraint on the number of active vertices and prior knowledge on specific vertices for sampling, mandatory inclusion or exclusion. We transformed this constrained problem into a difference-of-convex (DC) optimization problem by using the nuclear norm and a DC penalty for vertex selection. To solve this, we develop a convergent solver based on the general double-proximal gradient DC algorithm. The effectiveness of our method is demonstrated through experiments on various graph signal models, including real-world data, showing superior performance in the recovery accuracy compared to existing methods.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: IEEE Open Journal of Signal Processing, vol. 7, pp. 314-323, 2026
item.dc:creator: Keitaro Yamashita, Kazuki Naganuma, Shunsuke Ono

item.title: A general extractor for coherent patterns across time-frequency measurements
item.description: arXiv:2602.20317v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Scientific discovery increasingly depends on finding meaningful patterns within volumes of sensor data too large for manual inspection. Existing time-frequency event extractors are often engineered or trained on manually labeled examples for each instrument, which can be laborious and difficult to adapt to new environments. To address this, we introduce TokEye, a reference-free method that learns a general criterion for coherent structure from heterogeneous fusion measurements. A model developed under this method, without retraining, can extract signals from various other fields including marine bioacoustics and wideband radar. It recovers 82.5\% of expert-annotated stellarator signals, detects 78\% of dolphin whistles, and identifies radar events with 81.5\% average precision across six benchmarks, while processing full experimental spectrograms in under one second on a GPU. This transfer across unrelated sensors and physical systems reveals common exploitable structure in time-frequency measurements and establishes a scalable foundation for automated scientific signal discovery.
item.dc:creator: Nathaniel Chen, Kouroche Bouchiat, Peter Steiner, Andrew Rothstein, David Smith, Max Austin, Mike van Zeeland, Marie Roch, Azarakhsh Jalalvand, Egemen Kolemen

item.title: Programmable Unitary RF Networks for Narrowband Hybrid Beamforming
item.description: arXiv:2603.17616v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Conventional hybrid beamforming architectures are compared with one another and with the fully-digital architecture under the same radiated antenna power. However, the physically relevant power budget is the power supplied by the RF chains to the passive analog beamforming network, which then transfers it to the antenna ports. Some architectures, such as fully-connected architectures, can divert part of this power to terminated ports even under ideal passive-component assumptions, thereby delivering less power to the antenna ports than that supplied by the RF chains. Other architectures, such as partially connected architecture, transfer all RF-chain power to the antenna ports but have restricted beamforming flexibility and therefore do not attain the fully-digital sum-rate optimum in general. Motivated by this RF-chain injected-power and beamforming flexibility viewpoint, this paper proposes a hybrid beamforming architecture that, under ideal passive-component assumptions: i) transfers all RF-chain injected power to the antenna ports without loss; and ii) with continuous phase control and sufficiently many programmable phase layers, attains the fully-digital sum-rate optimum under the same RF-chain injected-power constraint. The proposed hybrid beamforming architecture uses a programmable unitary analog beamforming network realized by interlacing fixed mixing layers with programmable diagonal phase-shifting layers. We compare this architecture with fully-connected, partially connected, and Butler/DFT beam-selection baselines under ideal passive-component assumptions and show numerically that none of these baselines attains the fully-digital sum-rate optimum under the same RF-chain injected-power constraint. Finally, we compare the different architectures when component losses are taken into account and illustrate the balance between beamforming flexibility and accumulated losses.
item.dc:creator: Nikola Zlatanov, Damir Salakhov

item.title: Diffusion Models for Radio Map Estimation: Theoretical Performance Analysis and Sampling Rate Guideline
item.description: arXiv:2606.25310v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Radio maps, which characterize the spatial distribution of radio frequency metrics, such as the received signal strength, are essential for a wide range of wireless applications. The problem of radio map estimation involves constructing a radio map from a limited set of radio samples measured by sparsely distributed sensors.Recently, diffusion models have been increasingly adopted for this problem, yet their theoretical performance remains largely unexamined. Consequently, it is difficult to evaluate their performance when ground-truth radio maps are unavailable, as is often the case in practice. To bridge this gap, we first formulate radio map estimation as a non-linear matrix completion problem. We then derive a theoretical expression for the estimation error of a diffusion model, capturing the effects of the mismatch between the training and deployment environments, the model design, and the sampling strategy on the quality of the estimated radio map. Moreover, considering that the derived error expression depends on certain information that is difficult to obtain in practice, we propose an empirical approximation that is readily computable from observable data. Finally, extensive simulations demonstrate that the empirical formula closely approximates the theoretical error expression, validating its effectiveness for practical deployment. Our results provide guidelines not only for evaluating the performance of a diffusion model when ground truth is unavailable, but also for determining how many sensors are required to spatially sample the region to achieve a given estimation accuracy. They further reveal a critical sensor count beyond which the estimation performance of diffusion models converges.
item.dc:creator: Zhiyuan Liu, Qingyu Liu, Shuhang Zhang, Hongliang Zhang, Lingyang Song

item.title: Active STAR-RIS-Aided RSMA IoT Systems: Performance Analysis, Model-Based and Data-Driven Resource Allocation Frameworks
item.description: arXiv:2609.06429v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: STAR-RISs have emerged as a promising technology for achieving full-space signal coverage with low hardware complexity and energy consumption. In parallel, RSMA offers a flexible interference management mechanism that enhances spectral efficiency and user fairness. Integrating STAR-RIS with RSMA provides strong potential for robust and energy-efficient communications; however, the resulting double-fading cascaded channels and the inherent imbalance between near and far users pose reliability and fairness challenges. This study presents comprehensive information-theoretic and optimization frameworks for active STAR-RIS-assisted RSMA Internet-of-Things systems. Closed-form expressions for the OP and EC are derived under both the presence and absence of direct links. Based on these results, asymptotic OP and EC, diversity order, and array gain are analyzed to characterize system behavior. In addition, throughput-based and spectral-based energy efficiency metrics are investigated to quantify the tradeoffs between transmission performance and power consumption. To enhance user fairness, a fairness-oriented RA framework is developed to jointly optimize power allocation and rate-splitting coefficients using successive convex approximation and block coordinate descent techniques. To further improve scalability and real-time applicability, we introduce a data-driven RA framework based on DMNN, CMNN, and MXGB. This framework approximates the optimization-based solutions with substantially reduced computational complexity. Numerical results show that the proposed MXGB model achieves the shortest execution time while maintaining performance comparable to ground-truth-based benchmarks. Extensive Monte Carlo simulations validate the analytical results and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed frameworks.
item.dc:creator: Ngo Hoang Tu, Vo Nguyen Quoc Bao, Tran Thien Thanh

item.title: Revolutionizing 6G Wireless Networks with RISs: Enhancements in Sensing and Communications
item.description: arXiv:2610.27695v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) have emerged as one of the most promising technologies for the next-generation wireless networks, offering advantages such as cost efficiency, low power consumption, flexible deployment, and large effective aperture. Extensive studies have demonstrated the capabilities of RISs to enhance communication performance, including coverage extension, sum-rate improvement, interference suppression, security enhancement, etc. As 6G networks continue to evolve, wireless sensing is expected to play a pivotal role alongside communication. Undoubtedly, RISs possess great potential to enable seamless integration of sensing and communication by supporting both passive and active sensing paradigms. This paper explores how RISs can revolutionize wireless networks by enhancing both communication and sensing capabilities. Specifically, we highlight the fundamental principles, potential applications, and future trends of RIS-assisted integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), anticipating that RIS-enabled ISAC will become a key enabler in the upcoming 6G era.
item.dc:creator: Jiguang He, Yuwen Cao, Charles Vanwynsberghe, Aymen Fakhreddine, Yi Fang, Chongwen Huang, George C. Alexandropoulos, Merouane Debbah

item.title: Protocol Data Unit Header Decoding and Payload Coding Recovery in the Starlink Ku-Band Downlink
item.description: arXiv:2610.29387v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Existing Starlink downlink studies describe synchronization, pilots, and predictable waveform elements, but these descriptions do not establish how received header bits specify payload allocations and channel coding. Using 18 frames from one continuous complex-baseband capture spanning approximately 24 ms, we identify two protocol data unit (PDU) header regions in each frame and decode their contents after receiver correction and reference-phase removal. We recover the headers' terminated rate-1/3 convolutional code with constraint length seven and an eight-bit cyclic redundancy check over the concatenated information words. The decoded bits support a conditional 20-bit layout of modulation and coding scheme (MCS) index--length pairs, linking format labels and quantities to subsequent payload regions. Predicted allocation endpoints agree with signal-based estimates in 16 of 18 frames and differ by at most two symbols in the remaining frames. We further recover modulation mappings and equivalent quasi-cyclic low-density parity-check coding relations for several payload formats, including rate-1/2 and rate-5/8 families. Fixed generators predict 78,848, 9,984, and 811,008 parity bits for formats 5, 9, and 21 without disagreement on codewords excluded from their generator fitting. Cross-modulation tests support shared encoders. Formats 28 and 37 have verified shortened cores, with 256 and 384 additional bits unexplained, while format 68 remains unresolved.
item.dc:creator: Haoyan Liu, Yichuan Ma, Haotong Zhao, Chengguang Li, Min Yang

item.title: Bodyseismography (BSG): Theoretical Foundation and Numerical Modeling
item.description: arXiv:2610.35844v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Bodyseismography (BSG) records cardiovascular vibrations transmitted through the body and a supporting bed, enabling contactless assessment of cardiac mechanics. Relating these vibrations to hemodynamic features requires separating cardiac excitation from the effects of body and bed transmission. We develop a source-transmission-measurement framework that couples myocardial contraction and vascular recoil to directional BSG observations. The theory connects stroke volume, cardiac output, and blood pressure to observation and target Jacobians, establishes a local first-order target-observability criterion, and characterizes how additional sensing axes reduce ambiguities under specified source and transmission uncertainties. Numerical modeling combines four-chamber cardiac mechanics, cardiac-to-body excitation, and calibrated body-bed operators. Across 27 participants, a multilayer finite-element model with calibrated frequency correction achieves median Pearson correlation coefficients of 0.865 for the vertical channel and 0.682 for the planar-sum channel in matched-window waveform reconstruction. Controlled stroke-volume perturbations show that transmission reshapes feature sensitivity, including a reversal of the vertical feature association in 8 of 27 participant-specific transfer models. These analytical and numerical studies explain how cardiovascular sources and mechanical propagation jointly shape triaxial BSG and provide a physical basis for relating directional vibration features to hemodynamic changes.
item.dc:creator: Yuanyuan Zhang, Yuyan Wu, Sahas Biddappa, Yida Zhang, Jiayu Chen, Zixuan Zeng, Yixuan Li, Jiahui Li, Fei Dou, Zhenlin An, Younghoon Kwon, Hae Young Noh, WenZhan Song

item.title: Finite-Length Empirical Comparison of Polar, PAC, and Invertible-Extractor Secrecy Codes over the Wiretap BSC
item.description: arXiv:2604.19909v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We compare three secrecy-coding schemes for the degraded wiretap binary symmetric channel (BSC) in the finite-blocklength regime: (i) polar wiretap coset codes, (ii) PAC codes used as wiretap coset codes, and (iii) the invertible-extractor (IE) framework of Bellare--Tessaro. Our comparison is empirical and uses a common semantic-secrecy metric (distinguishing advantage). For polar coset codes, we compute Eve's polarized bit-channel capacities (via the Tal--Vardy construction) to obtain explicit finite-length upper bounds on mutual-information leakage, yielding strong secrecy bounds. For PAC coset codes, we prove that Eve's synthesized bit-channels are equivalent to those of polar codes (up to a permutation), so the same leakage bounds apply; we then convert these strong-secrecy bounds into semantic-secrecy guarantees for symmetric wiretap channels. For the IE scheme, we use the closed-form semantic-secrecy bounds already established. Finally, we report finite-length results that jointly characterize (a) semantic-secrecy guarantees against Eve and (b) frame-error-rate performance at Bob. Our simulations indicate that Polar and PAC codes exhibit comparable reliability performance under the considered finite-length settings, while PAC codes retain the same secrecy bounds as Polar codes. More broadly, our results highlight that non-universal designs of wiretap codes provide tighter secrecy guarantees than universal design based on invertible extractors.
item.dc:creator: Jaswanthi Mandalapu, Tyler Kann, Andrew Thangaraj, Matthieu R. Bloch

item.title: Continuous-time nonlinear closed-loop in-memory computing for high-accuracy massive MIMO detection
item.description: arXiv:2607.02842v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Analog in-memory computing (IMC) has emerged as a promising approach for accelerating matrix operations by exploiting the intrinsic physics of memory arrays. To date, however, most IMC architectures have focused on linear algebra workloads in which computation is encoded in the equilibrium state of a physical system. Extending these principles to nonlinear optimization remains challenging and typically relies on iterative algorithms composed of repeated linear operations. Here, we introduce a continuous-time nonlinear closed-loop IMC architecture for box-constrained zero-forcing (BCZF) decoding in massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. The proposed architecture embeds the decoding problem directly within the dynamics of a nonlinear feedback network of memory arrays and supply-limited operational amplifiers, allowing solutions to emerge through continuous-time physical optimization. We derive a compact analytical model of the circuit and show that its trajectories minimize an equivalent energy function. Experimental emulation using a fabricated IMC chip confirms the predicted dynamics under realistic hardware nonidealities for up to 16x16 MIMO systems. To overcome the finite precision of analog hardware, we extend mixed-precision iterative refinement from linear algebra to nonlinear continuous-time optimization, enabling reliable detection of high-order modulation formats including 1024-QAM. Benchmark projections indicate operation from ultra-low-energy approximate decoding to high-accuracy massive MIMO detection. Together, these results extend closed-loop IMC from equilibrium-based linear algebra to continuous-time nonlinear optimization and establish a pathway toward efficient physical accelerators for high-accuracy wireless communications.
item.dc:creator: Piergiulio Mannocci, Giacomo Pedretti, Giacomo Larelli, Fabian B\"ohm, Thomas Van Vaerenbergh

item.title: Discovering shared interpretable operations in image compression autoencoders
item.description: arXiv:2607.04839v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: With the increasing adoption of deep learning for applications such as image compression, improvements in the rate-distortion trade-off have been achieved at the cost of increasingly larger and more opaque ''black-box'' models. Autoencoders are among the most widely used architectures for this task; however, without a clear understanding of their internal behavior, these models tend to grow in complexity to achieve more performance gains. In this paper, we investigate whether universal behaviors can be detected from the internal operations of bias-free autoencoders through Jacobian analysis. If such behaviors exist, they may be extracted to design low-complexity image compression models inspired by high-complexity deep learning architectures.
item.dc:creator: Caroline Mazini Rodrigues (COMPACT), Nicolas Keriven (COMPACT), Thomas Maugey (Inria-EPFL, COMPACT)

item.title: The LQ Digital Mode Family: Protocol Architecture and Reference Specification for Weak-Signal Communications
item.description: arXiv:2609.06427v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper introduces LQ8, an open-source weak-signal digital mode for amateur radio that completes structured two-way contacts in 4 transmissions (60 s), achieving a 1.50x speedup over canonical 6-transmission exchanges (90 s) and 1.25x over 5-transmission RR73 exchanges (75 s) while preserving complete bidirectional exchange of Maidenhead grid locators, signal reports, and mutual acknowledgments. By replacing fixed-width message-type headers with variable-length prefix codes matched to physical-layer bit budgets, LQ8 packs the answering station's grid locator and measured signal report into a single 77-bit reply. In multi-station pileup operations, LQ8 confirms up to two answering stations simultaneously within a single-carrier 50.0 Hz transmission with a 0.0 dB RF power-splitting penalty, achieving a peak rate of 240 QSOs/h in continuous pileup (4x over single-carrier FT8; 480 QSOs/h dual-carrier) while retaining -21.0 dB SNR sensitivity. The protocol family also defines three extended profiles (LQ16, LQ4, and LQ2) tailored for extreme sensitivity, VHF/UHF contesting, and fast-burst channels.
item.dc:creator: Luis Quesada

item.title: Differentiable Systematic Resampling for Variational Sequential Monte Carlo
item.description: arXiv:2610.12094v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Particle filters are a standard tool for nonlinear state estimation, but their resampling step is discrete, preventing gradient-based learning in variational sequential Monte Carlo. We introduce Differentiable Systematic Resampling (DSR), a temperature-controlled relaxation of systematic resampling, that preserves the CDF-ordered, banded structure of systematic resampling while enabling full gradient flow. DSR converges to exact systematic resampling as the temperature vanishes, and we prove a pointwise exponential convergence rate for the induced bias. Compared to optimal-transport-based differentiable resampling, DSR avoids iterative solvers and has substantially lower computational overhead. Experiments on stochastic dynamical systems and real-world handwriting data show that DSR achieves comparable or superior filtering and dynamics learning performance.
item.dc:creator: Fredrik Cumlin, Saikat Chatterjee
